items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-03-22
items.q: No, I heard. Oh, yeah. Robert Mitchum came when he was in town. And he wound up at the Dewdrop.

ctx.x: Were there any problems with whites going to the Dewdrop?

No. The police was more problems than anybody else. Because they was the one that would try to keep people out. You know, Robert Mitchum came to the Dewdrop. No, I heard. Oh, yeah. Robert Mitchum came when he was in town. And he wound up at the Dewdrop. They tried to get him out. He told them they'd better go fly a kite. They had a priest. He used to come to the Dewdrop every Monday evening. You talking about that? He'd get drunk? Yeah. He would get him in his, him in the black lady. I don't know who the lady, I…
Were any of the whites arrested by the police? Do you remember?
